themes_detail.label: Noise at Houses of Worship
themes_detail.summary: Complaints about noise from houses of worship in CD 308 spiked to 4 this week, up 3100% from a 0.1 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 11.72), suggesting a sudden, acute disruption affecting a historically quiet category of 311 calls.
evidence: 4 complaints filed this week vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
z-score of 11.72 indicates statistically extreme spike
Complaint type has historically been negligible in this district
reporting_angles: Interview affected congregants and clergy about what changed this week and whether ongoing construction, equipment failure, or new programming is the cause
Check if multiple houses of worship (different denominations, locations) reported simultaneously, suggesting a single triggering event vs. isolated incident

themes_detail.label: Public Drinking Complaints Surge
themes_detail.summary: Public drinking complaints jumped to 3 this week, a 700% increase from the 0.4 weekly baseline over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 5.42), marking an emerging public-order signal in Crown Heights/Prospect Heights.
evidence: 3 complaints filed this week vs. 0.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
z-score of 5.42 indicates high statistical significance
First notable cluster in this complaint category for the district in recent period
reporting_angles: Canvass specific blocks where complaints were filed to identify if a particular venue, park, or corner is the hotspot
Interview NYPD about whether precinct enforcement or outreach has changed; cross-check against arrest data

themes_detail.label: Tree Maintenance Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Two related environmental spikes converged this week and last week: 6 dead/dying tree complaints this week (up 1100% from 0.5 weekly average, z-score 11.0) and 6 new tree requests last week (up 1500% from 0.4 weekly average, z-score 8.08), indicating urgent canopy stress or blight in the district.
evidence: 6 dead/dying tree complaints this week vs. 0.5 weekly average (1100% spike, z-score 11.0)
6 new tree requests last week vs. 0.4 weekly average (1500% spike, z-score 8.08)
5 overgrown tree/branch complaints this week vs. 0.8 weekly average (567% spike, z-score 5.13)
Convergence of three tree-related categories suggests district-wide canopy issue
reporting_angles: Partner with NYC Parks to identify which trees are dying and why—disease, pest infestation, drought stress, deferred maintenance?
Interview longtime residents about whether tree health has visibly deteriorated; check for recent major storms, construction, or utility work that could have triggered damage
Investigate whether CD 308 budget requests for park reconstruction/upgrade (recurrent multi-year ask) include canopy renewal; why hasn't it been funded?

themes_detail.label: Elevator Failures Spike
themes_detail.summary: Elevator complaints surged to 13 last week, a 271% increase from a 3.5 weekly baseline over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 5.27), with a separate spike of 3 elevator complaints this week (700% above baseline, z-score 5.42), indicating widespread building system failures affecting residents' access and mobility.
evidence: 13 elevator complaints last week vs. 3.5 weekly average (271% spike, z-score 5.27)
3 elevator complaints this week vs. 3.5 weekly average (700% spike, z-score 5.42)
Sustained pressure across two consecutive weeks suggests systemic issue, not one-off failure
Heat/hot water (1745 complaints over 90 days) and plumbing (520) also remain high, suggesting broader building maintenance crisis
reporting_angles: Obtain DOB elevator inspection records for CD 308 buildings filed in last 30 days; cross-reference with 311 data to identify if complaints cluster in specific buildings or blocks
Interview building owners/managers and elevator maintenance contractors about what caused the cluster—shortage of parts, technician availability, aging equipment?
Talk to elderly and disabled residents about how elevator outages impact their ability to access apartments, medical care, and services

themes_detail.label: Street Infrastructure Decay
themes_detail.summary: Missing street signs jumped to 3 complaints 3 weeks ago (up 1100% from 0.2 weekly baseline, z-score 6.35), while street condition complaints remain elevated at 366 over 90 days, suggesting neglected public right-of-way maintenance and navigation hazards in the district.
evidence: 3 missing street sign complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.2 weekly average (1100% spike, z-score 6.35)
366 street condition complaints over 90-day period indicates persistent baseline problem
Illegal parking dominance (2327 complaints) suggests street management is underfunded or deprioritized
reporting_angles: Walk the district to document missing or damaged street signs; map which intersections are most affected and assess traffic/pedestrian safety risk
Contact NYC DOT to determine inspection frequency and replacement timeline for street signage in CD 308 and whether it meets citywide standards
